title: incremental-golden-signalizer-and-workload-autogen
creator: Ava Park
description: Goal: Reduce noise in our CI perf signals and make golden baselines adaptive to small controlled workload drift. This ticket delivers an ’incremental golden signalizer’ service and a workload-autogen pipeline that synthesizes reproducible, variant-weighted traffic for prefill+decode paths. The focus is kernel selection and attention-optim optimizations: creating minimal-change runs that isolate kernel routing decisions and prefill/decode scheduling trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic golden-run generator that produces reproducible mixed workloads (short chat, long completion, streaming) with seed locking
Golden baselines are stored with metadata (kernel routing matrix, quantization profile, batch distribution, KV hit-rate) and can be diffed programmatically
CI perf gate detects >3% median token latency regression or >5% p99 regression on nightly runs and fails the pipeline with contextual run diffs
A smoke dashboard that surfaces top contributing kernels and prefill vs decode latency split per golden run
Integration tests for the autogen pipeline that validate sample-weight preservation and seed reproducibility
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ava Park: Initial kickoff. Spike ran 50 golden seeds across two instance types; observed kernel routing flip on ~7% of runs when sequence length variance increased. Decided to try deterministic seed locking + controlled jitter injection to make diffs more interpretable.

2026-03-04 - Diego Morales: Implemented prototype autogen that takes a weighted corpus and emits a seed bundle with traffic mixing ratios. Early results show stable median but noisy p99; next step is to add KV cache priming stages to reduce tail variance.
2026-03-06 - Priya Shah (SRE): Noted CI timing variability due to background cluster compaction jobs at 02:00 UTC. Suggested stagger runs and tag noisy hosts to avoid false positives in perf gates.

2026-03-08 - Diego Morales: Added kernel-matrix metadata to golden artifacts. Kernel-probing harness added to pinpoint which kernel variant was selected for each segment of the trace; helps attribute regressions to kernel routing vs microcode changes.

2026-03-10 - Design review (Liam Chen): Reviewed dashboard mockups — requested a compact diff view that highlights token-latency heatmap and top-3 contributing kernels. Assigned follow-up DES ticket for mockups.
